english.title: Public Nuisance - indecent exposure
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) committed a public nuisance by indecently exposing yourself by **(..SPECIFY THE MANNER OF THE EXPOSURE..)
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
indecently exposed him / her self

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence should only be used where other statutory offences do not cover the indecency.
(ii) The common law offence no longer applies from the 27th June 2022 and is replaced by a statutory offence of intentionally or recklessly causing public nuisance under section 78 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022, see H100671. Where exposure can be deemed as obstructing the public or a section of the public in the exercise or enjoyment of a right that may be exercised or, enjoyed by the public at large, the statutory nuisance offence may be considered. Alternatively, see the offence of exposure at H5816, pursuant to section 66 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
INDICTMENT: Imprisonment and / or a fine

Time Limit on Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
